arxiv-1903-03594.title: Cylindrical Films for Electronics in Low Background Physics Searches
arxiv-1903-03594.creator: J. Freedberg
arxiv-1903-03594.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by J. Freedberg. A technique for manufacturing thin-film resistors on cylindrical substrates is demonstrated. These devices are aimed for application in rare-event detectors that must minimize radioactive backgrounds from trace impurities in electronic components inside the detector. Cylindrical, conducting Ni films were created via Electron Beam Deposition, using a mechanism that rotates the substrate, to demonstrate proof of principle and measure the resistivity on axis and in azimuth.

arxiv-2102-00915.title: Traversable wormhole geometries in f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) gravity
arxiv-2102-00915.creator: Zinnat Hassan, Sanjay Mandal, P.K. Sahoo
arxiv-2102-00915.description: Abstract The current interests in the universe motivate us to go beyond Einstein’s General theory of relativity. One of the interesting proposals comes from a new class of teleparallel gravity named symmetric teleparallel gravity, i.e., f ⁡ ( Q ) f(Q) gravity, where the non-metricity term Q Q is accountable for fundamental interaction.

arxiv-2105-09450.title: Cosmic Velocity Field Reconstruction Using AI
arxiv-2105-09450.creator: Ziyong Wu, Zhenyu Zhang , Shuyang Pan, Haitao Miao, Xiaolin Luo, Xin Wang, Cristiano G. Sabiu, Jaime Forero-Romero, Yang Wang, Xiao-Dong Li
arxiv-2105-09450.description: Abstract We develop a deep learning technique to infer the non-linear velocity field from the dark matter density field. The deep learning architecture we use is an “U-net” style convolutional neural network, which consists of 15 convolution layers and 2 deconvolution layers.

arxiv-2109-14654.title: BEST Impact on Sterile Neutrino Hypothesis
arxiv-2109-14654.creator: Vladislav Barinov, Dmitry Gorbunov
arxiv-2109-14654.description: Abstract Recently the Baksan Experiment on Sterile Transitions (BEST) has presented results Barinov et al. 2021 confirming the gallium anomaly —a lack of electron neutrinos ν e \nu_{e} at calibrations of SAGE Abdurashitov et al. 1999 ; Abdurashitov et al. 2006 and GALLEX Kaether et al. 2010 —at the statistical significance exceeding 5 σ \sigma .

arxiv-2209-01031.title: GReS: Graphical Cross-domain Recommendation for Supply Chain Platform Conference: Proceedings of the 31th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management; October 17–21, 2022; Atlanta, GA, USA Proceedings of the 31th ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Mana
arxiv-2209-01031.creator: Zhiwen Jing, Ziliang Zhao, Yang Feng, Xaochen Ma, Nan Wu, Shengqiao Kang, Cheng Yang, Yujia Zhang, Hao Guo
arxiv-2209-01031.description: Abstract . Supply Chain Platforms (SCPs) provide downstream industries with raw materials. Compared with traditional e-commerce platforms, data in SCPs is more sparse due to limited user interests. To tackle the data sparsity problem, one can apply Cross-Domain Recommendation (CDR) to improve the recommendation performance of the target domain with the source domain information.

arxiv-2210-07699.title: s-Club Cluster Vertex Deletion on Interval and Well-Partitioned Chordal Graphs An extended abstract [ 12 ] of this paper was presented at WG 2022 and this version contains all proofs missing from the conference version.
arxiv-2210-07699.creator: Dibyayan Chakraborty, L. Sunil Chandran, Sajith Padinhatteeri, Raji. R. Pillai
arxiv-2210-07699.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the computational complexity of s s -Club Cluster Vertex Deletion . Given a graph, s s -Club Cluster Vertex Deletion ( s s -CVD) aims to delete the minimum number of vertices from the graph so that each connected component of the resulting graph has a diameter at most s s .

arxiv-2311-00445.title: A Systematic Comparison of Syllogistic Reasoning in Humans and Language Models
arxiv-2311-00445.creator: Tiwalayo Eisape, MH Tessler, Ishita Dasgupta, Fei Sha,, Sjoerd van Steenkiste, Tal Linzen, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Google DeepMind, Google Research
arxiv-2311-00445.description: Abstract A central component of rational behavior is logical inference: the process of determining which conclusions follow from a set of premises. Psychologists have documented several ways in which humans’ inferences deviate from the rules of logic. Do language models, which are trained on text generated by humans, replicate such human biases, or are they able to overcome them?

arxiv-2501-13109.title: Bayesian Model Parameter Learning in Linear Inverse Problems: Application in EEG Focal Source Imaging
arxiv-2501-13109.creator: Alexandra Koulouri, Ville Rimpiläinen
arxiv-2501-13109.description: Abstract Inverse problems are often described as limited-data problems in which the signal of interest cannot be observed directly. Therefore, a physics-based forward model that relates the signal with the observations is typically needed. Unfortunately, unknown model parameters and imperfect forward models can still undermine the signal recovery.

arxiv-2508-00463.title: Slow convergence almost everywhere of ergodic averages
arxiv-2508-00463.creator: Valery V. Ryzhikov
arxiv-2508-00463.description: Abstract For an ergodic action of the group Z^{n} on a probability space and a given arbitrarily slowly decreasing to zero sequence, there exists an integrable function such that the standard ergodic time averages for it converge almost everywhere to the spatial average of the function at a rate that is not asymptotically majorized by this sequence.

arxiv-2509-24583.title: The Complexity of Defining and Separating Fixpoint Formulae in Modal Logic
arxiv-2509-24583.creator: Jean Christoph Jung ORCID:0000-0002-4159-2255, Jędrzej Kołodziejski ORCID:0000-0001-5008-9224
arxiv-2509-24583.description: Abstract . Modal separability for modal fixpoint formulae is the problem to decide for two given modal fixpoint formulae φ , φ ′ \varphi,\varphi^{\prime} whether there is a modal formula ψ \psi that separates them, in the sense that φ ⊧ ψ \varphi\models\psi and ψ ⊧ ¬ φ ′ \psi\models\neg\varphi^{\prime} .

doe-osti-2589587-viscosity-measurements-.creator: Townsend, Joshua P., Boerner, Jeremiah James, Gardiner, Thomas Anthony et al.

However, current rad-hydro codes typically do not account for viscosity, which generally leads to large unc

pmc-10648114.title: Arthproliferins A–D, Four New Sesterterpenes from the Mangrove-Sediment-Derived Fungus Arthrinium sp. SCSIO41221
pmc-10648114.creator: Bin Yang, Cuitian Li, Ying Chen, Yanchun He, Jianglian She, Xuefeng Zhou, Huangming Tao, Bo Peng, Vincenzo Piccialli
pmc-10648114.description: Four new sesterterpenes, arthproliferins A–D (1–4), together with four known derivatives, were isolated and characterized from the mangrove-sediment-derived fungus Arthrinium sp. SCSIO41221. Their structures were determined using detailed nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) and mass spectroscopic (MS) analyses. Some of the isolated compounds were evaluated for their cytotoxicity in vitro.

pmc-11356986.title: Artemisinin and Its Derivatives as Potential Anticancer Agents
pmc-11356986.creator: Luan Wen, Ben Chung-Lap Chan, Ming-Hua Qiu, Ping-Chung Leung, Chun-Kwok Wong, Anna Ramunno, Francesca Aiello
pmc-11356986.description: Artemisinin is a natural sesquiterpene lactone obtained from the traditional Chinese medicinal herb Artemisia annua L. (qinghao). Artemisinin and its derivatives share an unusual endoperoxide bridge and are extensively used for malaria treatment worldwide. In addition to antimalarial activities, artemisinin and its derivatives have been reported to exhibit promising anticancer effects in recent decades.

pmc-11428582.title: Integrating Multi-Organ Imaging-Derived Phenotypes and Genomic Information for Predicting the Occurrence of Common Diseases
pmc-11428582.creator: Meng Liu, Yan Li, Longyu Sun, Mengting Sun, Xumei Hu, Qing Li, Mengyao Yu, Chengyan Wang, Xinping Ren, Jinlian Ma, Kwang Woo Ahn, Andrea Cataldo
pmc-11428582.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). As medical imaging technologies advance, these tools are playing a more and more important role in assisting clinical disease diagnosis. The fusion of biomedical imaging and multi-modal information is profound, as it significantly enhances diagnostic precision and comprehensiveness. Integrating multi-organ imaging with genomic information can significantly enhance the accuracy of disease prediction because many diseases involve both environmental and genetic determinants.

pmc-11466939.title: Case report: A rare case of neurocytoma of the Vth cranial nerve
pmc-11466939.creator: Yongping Gui, Fanghua Zhou, Bin Li, Bin Wu, Xingen Huang, Zhaomu Zeng, Shuhong Mei
pmc-11466939.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We report a case of neurocytoma originating from cranial nerve V. A 53-year-old female patient presented with a 20-day history of right frontotemporal facial paresthesia and pain. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed a 2.5-cm × 1.4-cm “dumbbell” enhancing lesion located in the cisternal segment of cranial nerve V with extension into Meckel’s cave, and the signal characteristics were suggestive of trigeminal neurinoma. The lesion was resected through a subtemporal middle cranial fossa approach.

pmc-11713134.title: A weakly‐supervised, MRI‐guided clustering of cognitive decline: A post‐hoc analysis of the EXPEDITION‐3 clinical trial
pmc-11713134.creator: Bhargav Teja Nallapu, Kellen K Petersen, Idris Demirsoy, Richard B Lipton, Christos Davatzikos, Laura Rabin, S Ahmad Sajjadi, Ali Ezzati
pmc-11713134.description: BackgroundAlzheimer's disease exhibits heterogeneity through varied phenotypic and pathological manifestations. Here, we aimed to investigate the potential of semi‐supervised pattern classification applied to volumetric MRI data in identifying relatively homogeneous subgroups of individuals exhibiting cognitive decline (CD) throughout the study period.MethodWe used data from the placebo arm of trial of Solanezumab for mild dementia due to AD (EXPEDITION‐3 trial).

pmc-12492768.title: Malaria in pregnancy: a holistic exploration of synergistic association through environmental, sociocultural, and socioeconomic lenses in Pru east municipality, Ghana
pmc-12492768.creator: Dennis Bardoe, Daniel Hayford, Robert Bagngmen Bio, Ernest Osei
pmc-12492768.description: BackgroundMalaria in pregnancy (MiP) is responsible for several maternal and neonatal complications. Despite the renewed dedication towards elimination and eradication, it is still endemic in Ghana. Although previous studies have examined MiP from clinical or epidemiological standpoints, gaps remain in understanding the interactions between determinants of transmission.

pmc-12515010.title: Hairdressers as Mental Health Gatekeepers in Adolescent Sextual Reproductive Health Contexts in Northern Uganda
pmc-12515010.creator: Amir Kabunga, Viola Nalwoga, Eustes Kigongo, Carolyn Stoney, Derick Modi, Udho Samson, Maxson Kenneth Anyolitho, Odette Murara, Bernard Omech
pmc-12515010.description: BackgroundAdolescents aged 10–19 in sub-Saharan Africa face overlapping sexual, reproductive, and mental health challenges, exacerbated by stigma, poverty, and limited youth-friendly services. Despite the documented intersection between adolescent sexual and reproductive health (SRH) and mental health, integrated interventions remain scarce, especially in resource-limited settings like Northern Uganda.

pmc-12540449.title: Rethinking neuropsychological test validity in dementia assessment: a critical review in the age of neuroimaging and digital markers
pmc-12540449.creator: Seyul Kwak
pmc-12540449.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Neuropsychological tests are essential tools for evaluating dementia and related neurocognitive disorders, with their clinical utility determined mainly by their validity. This paper critically reviews the diverse evidence supporting the validity of neuropsychological tests in dementia assessment. Criterion validity is discussed in relation to the tests’ ability to predict clinical diagnoses and underlying brain pathology, with a focus on their sensitivity to functional impairments and progressive neuropathological changes.

pmc-12623155.title: Mesoscopic vascular alterations in Alzheimer's disease
pmc-12623155.creator: Mackenzie Hyman, Shuaibin Chang, Dayang Gong, Etienne Chollet, Jiarui Yang, Anna Novoseltseva, Ayman A Abdelhakeem, Gϋlce Kϋreli, Shuying Li, Josh Bevan, Janice Weinberg, Patrick R Hof, Ann C McKee, Irving J Bigio, David A Boas, Bertrand R Huber, Hui Wang
pmc-12623155.description: INTRODUCTIONCerebrovascular alterations are associated with the pathology of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Yet, the role of these alterations is not fully understood, partly due to a paucity of data from mesoscopic vasculature (24–240 µm diameter).METHODSWe used label‐free, serial‐sectioning optical coherence tomography to reconstruct mesoscopic cerebrovasculature of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) samples from AD and control subjects.

pmc-12626273.title: Library size-stabilized metacells construction enhances co-expression network analysis in single-cell data
pmc-12626273.creator: Tianjiao Zhang, Haibin Zhu, Marcel Schulz, Marcel Schulz, Marcel Schulz, Marcel Schulz, Marcel Schulz
pmc-12626273.description: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) deciphers cell type-specific co-expression networks to resolve biological functions but remains constrained by data sparsity and compositional biases. Conventional metacells construction strategies mitigate sparsity by aggregating transcriptionally similar cells but often neglect systematic biases introduced by compositional data. This problem leads to spurious co-expression correlations and obscuring biologically meaningful interactions.

pmc-12787914.title: An Open and Novel Low-Cost Terrestrial Laser Scanner Prototype for Forest Monitoring
pmc-12787914.creator: Jozef Výbošťok, Juliána Chudá, Daniel Tomčík, Dominik Gretsch, Julián Tomaštík, Michał Pełka, Janusz Bedkowski, Michal Skladan, Martin Mokroš
pmc-12787914.description: Highlights What are the main findings? The low-cost TLS prototype was constructed for less than EUR 2050.All hardware components are publicly available, enabling easy construction. What are the implications of the main findings? Full build documentation will be shared on Zenodo.

pmc-13066887.title: Radiomic analysis of medical imaging for classification in oncology and recommendations for clinically initiated research: a literature review
pmc-13066887.creator: Kaijing Mao, Lun Matthew Wong, Kuo Feng Hung, Rongli Zhang, Walter Y H Lam, Zhiyi Shan, Tiffany Y So, Qi Yong Hemis Ai, Kyongtae Ty Bae
pmc-13066887.description: Background and ObjectiveRadiomics is a thriving field that aims to enhance clinical decision-making by enabling the noninvasive, quantitative characterization of lesions on medical images. Despite thousands of studies being published in this field, the adaptation of radiomics in routine clinical practice remains challenging due to the complexity of analytical steps and issues in reproducibility.

pmc-13376850.title: Value and Credibility of Meta-Analysis: Tutorial on Enhancing Methodological Rigor and AI-Powered Efficiency
pmc-13376850.creator: Stefano Brini, Tiffany I Leung
pmc-13376850.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The value of a meta-analysis is based on its methodological and statistical rigor, yet many published systematic reviews and meta-analyses contain statistical shortcomings that limit their utility for clinical practice and public health. This can make it challenging to aggregate data for treatment choices for patients as well as limit the extent to which policymakers can promote social change and improve public health.

pmc-13455368.title: Polyunsaturated fatty acid and oxylipin profiles of Angiostrongylus cantonensis during cerebral-to-pulmonary migration illuminate parasite and host microenvironmental lipid signatures
pmc-13455368.creator: Zhengxu Tang, Jiaying Lai, Yashan Song, Song Li, Lihua Xiao, Yaoyu Feng, Dongjuan Yuan
pmc-13455368.description: BackgroundMetabolic streamlining as a consequence of parasitism has resulted in the loss of lipid biosynthetic genes in nematodes. Angiostrongylus cantonensis, a zoonotic neurotropic parasite that causes eosinophilic meningitis in mammals, completes a complex migration through the rat brain before maturing in the pulmonary arteries.

pmc-13494028.title: HMGA2 identified via m6A-senescence multi-omics in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-13494028.creator: Meng Jin, Lingmei Qu, Zhaonan Xu, Shuang Teng, Shuo Liu, Qiuying Li, Fengshuo Zhang, Qing Hao, Peng Wang, Rui Zhao, Bingrui Yan, Yanan Sun
pmc-13494028.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification and cellular senescence have been individually implicated in tumor biology, but the landscape of m6A-related senescence genes in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) remains underexplored. In this study, we conducted an integrated multi-omics analysis combining bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, somatic mutation and copy number variation data, and proteomics to explore the clinical and molecular impacts of m6A-related senescence.

pmc-13679315.title: Biomarkers of subclinical cholestasis predict cancer immunotherapy outcomes
pmc-13679315.creator: Anne-Laure Mallard de La Varende, Marine Fidelle, Guido Kroemer, Laurence Zitvogel
pmc-13679315.description: In a recent paper published in Cancer Cell, we identified subclinical cholestasis as an accessible imprint of gut dysbiosis predicting resistance to immune checkpoint blockade. Our work connects γ-glutamyl transferase, bile-acid remodeling, and MAdCAM-1 loss to compromised antitumor immunity, opening avenues for novel biomarker-guided microbiota interventions.

pmc-13722873.title: Development and application of a 40K liquid chip enriched with structural variation markers for watermelon breeding
pmc-13722873.creator: Mingxia Zhao, Rui Cheng, Yongchun Wang, Jisheng Liu, Xiaoni Li, Lifang Xue, Taohong Fang, Yudong Sun, Yun Deng, Yunbi Xu, Xingping Zhang
pmc-13722873.description: Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) has undergone severe loss of genetic diversity due to domestication, necessitating the exploitation of wild relatives for trait improvement. While structural variations (SVs) represent a major source of genetic diversity, high-throughput SV genotyping remains technically challenging, and existing single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) arrays fail to capture presence/absence variations (PAVs) that differentiate wild from cultivated germplasm.
